assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36)amide) led to incretin therapies that transformed diabetes care and obesity treatment. The discovery chain runs from mechanism to widely used drugs with large clinical effect, giving a rare combination of physiological originality and measurable benefit to patients.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor signaling, preclinical-to-clinical translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form) are the strongest basic-science trio. Knudsen's drug-design contribution is substantial but a different kind of contribution; Habener and others are not on the supplied list, so the credit picture is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and large outcome trials; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, with the field still expanding.
uncertainties: Priority disputes around the identification of the active GLP-1 form and the role of other groups not on the list.
Whether a basic-science prize should also include the pharmaceutical development (Knudsen) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into interferon and inflammatory responses. It unified antiviral defense, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence under one mechanism and introduced cyclic dinucleotide second messengers (cGAMP) in metazoan immunity. Originality and conceptual clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger 2'3'-cGAMP, the decisive biochemical step; Barber identified STING (as MITA/ERIS-era work was independent) and its role in DNA-triggered innate immunity. Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are real contributors but the two-person configuration is the cleanest defensible one.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and structural work; clinical therapeutics (STING agonists/antagonists) are still maturing, but the mechanistic discovery is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Separate and near-simultaneous discovery of STING by several groups complicates credit.
Clinical translation is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling, with IRE1-mediated unconventional splicing of HAC1/XBP1 mRNA. It is conceptually clean, broadly conserved, and relevant to secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. As an RNA-processing mechanism it is also scientifically elegant.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the pathway (Mori identified the UPR element and HAC1/ATF6 components, Walter identified IRE1 function and mRNA splicing). Credit is relatively clean and a two-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years of confirmation and clear textbook status; recognition is arguably overdue and the field is stable.
uncertainties: Contributions of others (e.g. Kohno, Ron, Sidrauski) in the extension to mammalian pathways are not on the supplied list.
Direct clinical translation is less developed than for therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified a neuropeptide system essential for stable wakefulness and established loss of orexin neurons as the cause of narcolepsy type 1, with direct therapeutic consequences (orexin receptor antagonists and agonists). It is a clear case of discovery with a tight link between molecule, circuit and disease.
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexins and receptors and the narcolepsy phenotype in knockouts; Mignot's canine narcolepsy gene positional cloning of the orexin receptor 2 mutation is decisive. De Lecea and Kilduff discovered hypocretin independently, so credit is contested and exceeds three names.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated; therapeutics are now emerging; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority overlap between the orexin and hypocretin discoveries makes a three-person limit contested.
Sleep-physiology prizes have been rare, so the field fit is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a method for causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision, built on microbial channelrhodopsins. The methodological impact across the life sciences is very large and there is early translational use in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth and Boyden established its use in neurons and behaving animals; Miesenböck contributed earlier genetically targeted photostimulation. With six credited names the three-person constraint makes fair credit hard.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted; clinical application is limited so far, but as a tool the impact is well established.
uncertainties: Disputed credit between the channelrhodopsin discovery and the neuronal application.
Whether a tool or method fits the prize criteria as strongly as a discovery with disease relevance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells gave durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality. Clinical impact is clear, with multiple approved products, and the idea of redirecting T cells with synthetic receptors is original.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28/4-1BB-costimulated CARs, preclinical proof), June (first clinical successes in CLL and costimulatory design) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cell trials) are the best-supported three. Eshhar and others are not on the list, which leaves credit incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is strong, though long-term safety, solid-tumor extension and manufacturing remain active issues.
uncertainties: Credit omission of early CAR concept work (not on the supplied list).
Long-term durability and toxicity data are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identified a central regulator of cell growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism, with consequences for cancer, diabetes, aging and immunosuppression. The discovery is both foundational and linked to clinical rapamycin-class therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genes and function in yeast; Schreiber (FKBP12-rapamycin target pull-down) and Sabatini (mTOR identification and mTORC1 nutrient sensing) are central to the mammalian chain. Heitman, Brown and others are important and not all are listed, so allocation is complex.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and stable; recognition is timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Complicated credit allocation across yeast genetics, chemical biology and mammalian biochemistry.
Contribution of individual candidates and personal circumstances affecting selection are not assessed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 linked a chromosomal translocation in lymphoma to inhibition of cell death, establishing apoptosis regulation as a mechanism of oncogenesis and leading to BH3-mimetic therapy (venetoclax) in leukemia. Importance and clinical consequence are high.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterized BCL-2 and its family; Vaux showed its anti-apoptotic function. Strasser extended the work. Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer (the latter deceased) are important for translocation cloning and are not on the list, so attribution is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Well established with approved drugs; the story is mature, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with the discovery of the t(14;18) translocation outside the supplied names.
Prior prizes for apoptosis (2002) may reduce novelty in the committee's view.
